summary: Tested new Interest flow end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_interests.py (18 pytest cases across TestSendInterest, TestListInterests, TestStatus, TestRespond, TestContactUnlock) — all 18 PASS when run serially (`-n 0`). Playwright UI test verified: (1) Send-Interest button on /search POSTs, shows search-toast 'Interest sent successfully', becomes disabled with label 'Interest Sent' + card shows 'Interest pending'; (2) Recipient sees interests-pending-badge=1 on tab-interests, accept-interest-* + decline-interest-* buttons present; (3) After Accept, buttons disappear and interest-contact-* chip shows mobile + email; (4) Sender opening search-profile modal sees modal-interest-accepted with 'Contact Unlocked' and real mobile displayed.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope; the shared MongoDB `interests` collection means classes running on different workers race (e.g. TestRespond.accept flips status to accepted while TestStatus.test_status_pending_sent still expects pending). Interest tests must therefore run with `-n 0`. Recommend either (a) using per-test unique target pairs so classes don't share state, or (b) documenting `-n 0` for these tests, or (c) using module-scoped ordering guarantees. Not a product bug, but a test-infra caveat.
server.py has grown past ~1050 lines; splitting into modules (auth, users, photos, interests, search) would improve maintainability.

In send_interest, duplicate detection currently ignores 'declined' state — sending again after decline still creates a new pending. This may or may not be the desired product behaviour (spec says idempotent for same target). Confirm with product.
list_received_interests / list_sent_interests execute N+1 queries (find_one per row). Fine at current scale, but consider $lookup for larger datasets.
